records.description: Add neighbour-size starts: cycle restarts through random, the n+1 optimum with its least-radius circle removed, and the n-1 optimum with a circle placed at the largest gap, each followed by SLSQP.
Add neighbour-size starts: cycle restarts through random, the n+1 optimum with its least-radius circle removed, and the n-1 optimum with a circle placed at the largest gap, each followed by SLSQP.

Adds a large-neighbourhood dropout move: with probability 0.5 after the first start, remove about 20% of the incumbent's circles, re-solve the rest by SLSQP from their current positions, reinsert the removed circles at random, and re-solve all circles.
Supply an analytic gradient for the SLSQP objective and an analytic Jacobian for the constraint vector (pairwise distance rows, boundary rows, radius rows) so SLSQP no longer uses finite differences.
Raise SLSQP MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 and set ftol to 1e-12 so each local solve converges fully instead of stopping early.

With probability 0.5, each start mirrors the second half of the centres across the vertical midline or the diagonal of the first half, so SLSQP begins from a symmetric configuration, while the rest keep plain random starts.

After an initial 30% of the time budget of random SLSQP restarts, run monotone basin hopping: perturb the incumbent centres with Gaussian noise (sigma 0.02 to 0.05), reset 0 to 2 random radii, re-solve with SLSQP from that point, and keep the result only if its repaired radius sum is higher.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The constraints and the repair step are unchanged, so the packings stay valid. One problem: each restart now maximises a weighted sum of radii, sum(w*r), not the true sum. If the restart loop picks the best result by res.fun and not by the true sum of radii, that pick is biased. This is a design flaw that lowers quality, not a measurement bug.

The result fits the change. Optimising the wrong objective should lower the sum of radii: the candidate got 2.6115 against the incumbent's 2.6280, a drop of about 0.0165, which is far larger than the noise.

Recomputed z = -0.0165 / (0.0023 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/10)) ≈ -6.84. The harness value of -6.882 agrees within the rounding of the shown values. The candidate is just one run, but the effect is so large that rejecting it is clearly right.

records.description: Radius-weighted restarts: each restart draws random weights w_i uniform in [0.5, 1.5] and runs SLSQP on sum(w_i * r_i), while the best packing is still chosen by the true unweighted sum after repair.
Each restart first maximises a common radius t with all radii tied equal (SLSQP over centres plus one scalar), then runs the full free-radius SLSQP from that equal-radius configuration.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and no use of labels. The change adds a warm-start phase that solves for equal radii and then runs the existing free-radius SLSQP from that point. This is a legitimate optimisation change.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Phase 1 clamps t to at least 0 before using it to seed phase 2. Phase 2 uses the same constraint function and objective as the incumbent. The repair step that follows is unchanged, so the harness's validity check still applies.

Recomputed z = (2.6311 - 2.6280) / (0.0023 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/10)) = 0.0031 / 0.001782 ≈ 1.74. The harness reports 1.783. That is within the range the 4-decimal rounding of the inputs allows (about 1.71 to 1.80), so it is consistent.
The evidence is borderline. There are only 2 candidate runs, and z ≈ 1.74–1.78 is just above a typical threshold. A replicate would make the accept safer.

Both candidate runs give exactly -2.6311 to 4 decimals. That is plausible if different seeds reach the same local optimum. The harness raised no integrity flags, but it would be worth confirming the seed really reaches the initial points (x0).

records.description: Each restart first maximises a common radius t with all radii tied equal (SLSQP over centres plus one scalar), then runs the full free-radius SLSQP from that equal-radius configuration.

Alternate restarts between a largest-hole insertion start (best n-1 packing plus one new circle at the grid point with the largest clearance, including walls) and the original random start, with the new circle's clearance as its initial radius.

Replaces the fresh-restart loop with a simulated-annealing walk: each step perturbs the current packing, re-solves the free-radius SLSQP from there, and accepts a worse packing with probability exp(-(old-new)/T), where T decays geometrically from 1e-2 to 1e-4 over the process_time budget, while the best packing found is returned.

Replaces the fresh-restart loop with a simulated-annealing walk: each step perturbs the current packing, re-solves the free-radius SLSQP from there, and accepts a worse packing with probability exp(-(old-new)/T), where T decays geometrically from 1e-2 to 1e-4 over the process_time budget, while the best packing found is returned.
Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so each solve uses about 16 percent more of its CPU budget for random restarts, with the remaining margin under the 45 s void limit.
Replace the greedy radius repair with an exact LP (linprog/HiGHS) that maximises sum(r) for fixed centres, keeping the original clamp and overlap-guard loop as a float-tolerance safety net.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.
No bug that makes the result meaningless. The harness's exact validity check and the existing repair step still run, so the reported sum is a valid packing.

Design weakness, not a veto: the random radii r0 are given to circles without regard to where phase 1 put them. Phase 1 balanced positions for equal radii, so the phase-2 start is probably badly infeasible and partly throws away phase 1's work. Drawing r0 first also shifts the rng stream used for x0, which adds confounding.

Recomputed z: the rounded means are equal (-2.6311 vs -2.6311), so z is about 0. Standard error = 0.0023*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.0028. The harness value of -0.023 matches a difference of about 6e-5 hidden by rounding. Nothing contradicts the reported numbers.
The evidence is weak: one candidate run against two incumbent runs. Rejecting is right because there is no detectable gain, and the change adds code.

records.description: Draw random initial radii uniformly in [0.01, 0.12], rescale them so the total circle area is 0.6, and use them as the starting radii for the free-radius SLSQP phase in place of the tied phase-1 radius.

After each random-restart local optimum, run 3 swap moves that exchange the centres of a large circle and its farthest small circle (radii kept in place), re-solve with free-radius SLSQP from that start, and keep the result only if it beats the current best.

Starts one in three restarts from a jittered square lattice of about n sites (random extras removed to reach exactly n), with the rest uniform random, to test whether lattice-like structure helps SLSQP reach better packings.

Before the equal-radius SLSQP phase, run five L-BFGS-B stages on -sum(r) + mu * sum(min(constraint, 0)^2) with mu going from 10 to 1e5 (factor 10 per stage), and use the resulting centres as the start for SLSQP.
On half of the restarts, place 4 circles evenly spaced (with random offsets) on each wall at the wall-distance INIT_RADIUS, fill the rest uniformly, then run the same two-phase SLSQP.
Vectorise constraint assembly with precomputed pair indices and reused buffers in cons and the Jacobian, as a pure speed-up.

Replace the last 70% of random restarts with remove-and-reinsert moves: delete the 1 or 2 smallest-radius circles from the incumbent, reinsert each at the largest empty spot among 2000 random candidates, then polish with SLSQP and repair.
Abort the over-inflation then deflation idea: it is another start-diversity tweak, and the notes say to skip those.
Project initial centres into [r, 1-r] and set starting radii to min(wall distance, 0.5 x nearest-neighbour distance) so SLSQP starts from a feasible point.

Phase 2 runs SLSQP in four stages with a random per-restart linear tilt eps*(a.x + b.y), where eps decays geometrically (0.05, 0.015, 0.0045) and the final stage uses eps=0 so the objective is exactly sum(r).

Adds an elite pool of the five best distinct packings, and with probability 0.5 (once two parents exist) seeds SLSQP with a crossover child made from the left half of one parent and the right half of another, fixing the count to n.
Median-stopping: after the first 10 restarts, skip the expensive phase-2 free-radius SLSQP for any restart whose phase-1 equal-radius value falls below the median of earlier phase-1 values.
Warm-restart the phase-2 free-radius SLSQP up to 5 times from its own output, stopping once the sum of radii gains less than 1e-9, with MAX_ITER and the time check unchanged.
Aborted: the Gaussian-smoothed L-BFGS-B overlap-penalty warm start is a close variant of slot 18, which ran L-BFGS-B penalty stages before the equal-radius SLSQP and came out worse (+0.0034).

Replaces the equal-budget restart loop with successive halving over a pool of 16 random starts (SLSQP maxiter 40, doubling to MAX_ITER with the top half kept each round, refilling when the pool is exhausted), keeping the process_time budget check and repairing the best result.

Replaces the fixed restart loop with a UCB1 bandit over four move types (fresh restart, Gaussian kick, slice-and-rotate, remove-and-reinsert of the smallest circle), rewarding 1 when a solve beats the incumbent and 0 otherwise, with each move still followed by the same SLSQP solve and repair.

After the first 20% of the budget of random restarts, run iterated local search from the incumbent: each kick adds Gaussian noise to every centre with sigma decaying geometrically from 0.08 to 0.001, then runs free-radius SLSQP and repair, accepting only improvements.

After the first 20% of the budget of random restarts, run iterated local search from the incumbent: each kick adds Gaussian noise to every centre with sigma decaying geometrically from 0.08 to 0.001, then runs free-radius SLSQP and repair, accepting only improvements.

Replace the phase-2 free-radius SLSQP with a trust-region sequential LP (linprog/HiGHS) that linearises all pair, wall and radius constraints around the current packing, accepts steps that improve the repaired sum of radii, and halves or grows the trust region accordingly.

Replace the hard-constraint phase-1 equal-radius SLSQP with a log-barrier continuation (mu from 1e-2 down to 1e-7, warm-started per stage, linear extension below gap 1e-6), then keep the original hard-constraint free-radius phase 2.

Abort: penalty-weighted objective annealing is a near-duplicate of slot 18 (L-BFGS-B penalty continuation before the equal-radius SLSQP, +0.0034) and of slot 30 (log-barrier continuation, +0.0045), both already rejected.
Abort soft-repulsion pre-spreading: it is a near-duplicate of the L-BFGS-B overlap-penalty warm start (slot 18, +0.0034, rejected) and the start-diversity direction the notes say to skip.

Adds a Langevin soft-disk annealing stage (geometric temperature 1e-2 to 1e-5 over 2000 noisy gradient steps, then an L-BFGS-B quench) between the equal-radius phase and the free-radius SLSQP, with radii fixed to the phase-1 value; the -lambda*sum(r) reward is omitted because it is constant when radii are fixed.

Add a greedy maximal-empty-circle start (2000 candidates per step, top-10 random pick with probability 0.5) used for one start in three, feeding its centres and radii directly into the phase-2 free-radius SLSQP.

issues: No integrity problems: the code reads no files and contains no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from rng = default_rng(seed). The final packing still goes through _repair, so validity is enforced the same way as in the incumbent.

Recomputed z: the difference is 2.6324 - 2.6311 = 0.0013. SE = 0.0023*sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) = 0.00282, so z = 0.46. The harness's 0.456 agrees (the gap is from rounding). That is one candidate run against two incumbent runs, a gain of about half a noise sd, and is not significant. Rejecting, or asking for a replicate, is consistent with the numbers.
Minor: _free rebuilds a free-radius SLSQP that probably duplicates the logic in _solve_once. Reusing that function would be simpler.

Minor: the deque window is never cleared after an amplitude adaptation. Once 20 entries are full, amp is rescaled on every iteration based on mostly the same acceptance history, so it can drift to AMP_MIN or AMP_MAX faster than the intended 1/5-rule behaviour. This is not a validity bug.
Minor: the time check runs only before each SLSQP call. The last call can run past the 24 s budget, but with n=26 a single call is unlikely to reach the 45 s void limit.
The acceptance threshold T (1e-3 down to 1e-6) is tiny next to the gains possible per step, so the 'annealing' is nearly greedy. That is a design observation, not a bug.

records.description: Replace the restart loop with a perturbation walk from the slot-8 incumbent packing, using a 1/5-style sliding-window rule (20 steps, thresholds 0.3 and 0.15, factors 1.2 and 0.8, clamp [1e-3, 0.1], start 0.02) to adapt the perturbation amplitude, and a threshold acceptance whose temperature decays geometrically from 1e-3 to 1e-6 over the budget.
Aborted the Lubachevsky-Stillinger growth-start idea: it is another start-diversity tweak, which the notes say to skip, and it would only change how phase 1 is initialised.
Soft-min gap continuation: before the phase-2 SLSQP, minimise -sum(r) plus a log-sum-exp soft-min of the gaps with L-BFGS-B while raising beta through 10 to 10000.

Adds a multiplier-guided move: after each local solve, an LP over the fixed centres gives radius duals, the lowest-sensitivity circle is moved to the largest hole on a 100x100 grid with probability 0.3, and the result is kept only if sum(r) improves.

Local disc re-randomisation kick: after one initial random restart, each iteration takes the best packing, re-randomises the centres of circles within a uniform radius R in [0.15, 0.35] of a random point (radii of those circles set to 0), runs the full phase-2 free-radius SLSQP from that state, repairs, and keeps the result if it improves the best.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff has no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. All randomness comes from the seeded rng, and _repair still runs on every result, so each packing is still checked and made valid.

z recomputed: candidate mean is -2.63485 over 2 runs and incumbent mean is -2.6311 over 2 runs, a difference of 0.00375. The standard error is 0.0023*sqrt(1/2+1/2) = 0.0023, which gives z = 1.63. The harness reports 1.640, and the gap is consistent with the displayed values being rounded to 4 decimals.

The evidence is borderline: z is about 1.6 with only 2 runs per arm. A replicate before committing would firm this up. Both candidate runs (2.6343 and 2.6354) beat the incumbent mean, so the direction looks real.

Minor, not a bug: when the kick disc contains no centres (k=0), the step just re-optimises the current best, which wastes some time. x0 is still drawn in _solve_once when a start is given, which consumes rng draws but does no harm.

Design note: after the first random start the search becomes pure local kicks around the best solution, so the result depends on that first basin. This is a valid design choice and not a measurement problem.

records.description: Local disc re-randomisation kick: after one initial random restart, each iteration takes the best packing, re-randomises the centres of circles within a uniform radius R in [0.15, 0.35] of a random point (radii of those circles set to 0), runs the full phase-2 free-radius SLSQP from that state, repairs, and keeps the result if it improves the best.

Replaces the single-chain restart/kick loop with four replica-exchange chains at temperatures 1e-3 to 3e-2 and Gaussian perturbation scales 0.01 to 0.2, with Metropolis acceptance on sum(r), adjacent-state swaps every 20 rounds, and the best packing seen by any chain returned.

After the first 30% of the time budget of random restarts, each step rotates the circles on one side of a random line through the square by a random angle in [-0.3, 0.3] rad about the line's point nearest the centre, clips centres into the square, and re-optimises with free-radius SLSQP, keeping the result only if it beats the incumbent.

Aborted: archive-stratified restart sampling is a start-diversity tweak, which the notes say to skip, and it closely duplicates the rejected elite-pool idea (slot 22) and the perturbation-walk idea (slot 33).
Abort: a phase-2 radius log-barrier continuation is a close variant of slot 30's log-barrier continuation, which hurt (+0.0045), so I am not spending a slot on it.

Two-island model: three independent chains, each seeded from a SeedSequence child, run the fresh-start-then-kick walk in round-robin time slices over four epochs, and at each epoch start every chain adopts the global best if it is strictly better than its own.

memo: Helped: changes to how each solve searches. Slot 8 (equal-radius SLSQP before the free solve) gave -2.6311/-2.6311. Slot 35 (local disc re-randomisation kick) is the incumbent at -2.6343/-2.6354 (delta -0.0037, 2 runs, mean -2.6349). Local-search walks beat fresh restarts: slot 11 gave -2.6354/-2.6334 and slot 27 gave -2.6341/-2.6324. Replica exchange (-2.6348) and the two-island model (-2.6349) tie the incumbent, so more chain machinery adds nothing. No effect (+0.0000): TIME_FRACTION 0.93, LP repair, warm restarts, successive halving. Hurt: radius-weighted restarts (+0.0165), log-barrier (+0.0045), L-BFGS-B penalty (+0.0034), MAX_ITER 1000 (+0.0019). Start-diversity tweaks are exhausted. Next: tune the kick size, disc radius and acceptance rule of slot 35, and polish the best packing at the end. Replicate any gain, since noise sd is 0.0023. Keep the code simple.

incumbent.description: Local disc re-randomisation kick: after one initial random restart, each iteration takes the best packing, re-randomises the centres of circles within a uniform radius R in [0.15, 0.35] of a random point (radii of those circles set to 0), runs the full phase-2 free-radius SLSQP from that state, repairs, and keeps the result if it improves the best.

backlog.spec: Supply a vectorized Jacobian to minimize via the jac argument, and for the constraint dict supply jac for cons(v), so SLSQP stops using finite differences. Compute pairwise derivatives of the distance terms with numpy broadcasting over the iu pairs (d/dc_i = (c_i - c_j)/d, d/dr_i = -1), and the boundary and radius constraints as constant or sparse rows. This cuts per-iteration cost sharply, so more restarts fit in the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Instead of all n(n-1)/2 pair constraints, include only pairs whose centres are closer than a cutoff (for example r_i + r_j + 0.2 at the start point), rebuilt every few SLSQP restarts or after each solve. Keep the boundary and radius constraints. This shrinks the constraint matrix so SLSQP runs faster, and a final check ensures no excluded pair overlaps, re-solving if it does.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy _repair loop with a linear program: with the centres fixed, maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= min(x_i, 1-x_i, y_i, 1-y_i), r >= 0, solved by scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). This gives the exact best radii for those centres, which is at least as good as the shrink repair and removes the need for SHRINK. Keep a tiny safety margin of 1e-12 so the double-precision check passes.
backlog.title: Exact LP for radii given centres

backlog.spec: After an initial batch of random SLSQP restarts, repeatedly take the current best packing, perturb the centres by Gaussian noise (sigma about 0.02 to 0.05) and optionally shrink or reset a random small subset of radii, then re-run SLSQP from the perturbed point. Accept the new packing only if its repaired sum of radii is higher. This is monotone basin hopping and uses the time budget on local refinement of good basins.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent best

backlog.spec: Maintain a current packing and perturb it as in basin hopping, but accept a worse candidate with probability exp(-(old - new)/T), where T decays geometrically from about 0.01 to 1e-4 over the time budget. Keep a separate best-so-far record that is returned. The temperature schedule is driven by elapsed process_time so it fits the budget regardless of how many iterations run.
backlog.title: Simulated-annealing acceptance over restarts

backlog.spec: Perturb the incumbent by picking the one or two smallest-radius circles, deleting them, and reinserting each at the point of largest empty space found by sampling about 2000 random candidate points and taking the one maximising the minimum distance to other circle boundaries and walls. Then run SLSQP from this configuration. This targets wasted space, which is the usual weakness of random restarts for circle packing.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert moves

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, relax the initial random centres with a cheap smooth energy: penalise pairwise overlap max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 plus boundary violations with equal radii about 0.5/sqrt(n), minimised by L-BFGS-B with an analytic gradient. Then start SLSQP from these well-spread centres with radii set to the feasible values. This gives a better starting basin than uniform random positions.
backlog.title: Soft-repulsion pre-spreading

backlog.spec: Generate some initial configurations from a hexagonal or square lattice with about n sites, chosen by taking the lattice points that fit in the unit square and then removing or adding random points to reach exactly n, with random small jitter (sigma about 0.01). Mix these with the uniform random starts, choosing lattice starts for a fixed fraction of restarts (for example one in three). Lattice-like structure is common in good packings for this size.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-lattice starting points

backlog.spec: Solve a sequence of unconstrained problems with L-BFGS-B: minimise -sum(r) + mu * (sum of squared constraint violations), increasing mu by a factor of 10 over about 5 stages from 10 to 1e5. Then pass the result to SLSQP as the starting point to polish the active constraints. The penalty stage is cheap and gives SLSQP a point that is already nearly feasible, so its iterations are fewer.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: In each restart, first solve the max-min-distance style problem: maximise a common radius t with all radii forced equal (one scalar variable plus centres), using SLSQP. Then release the radii as free variables and run the full SLSQP from that point. Equal-radius phase gives a well-spread configuration that the free-radius phase then grows unevenly, which is a different basin than random starts.
backlog.title: Two-phase SLSQP with equal-radii start

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the best five distinct packings found so far. For each new restart, with probability 0.5 build a child by taking the circles in the left half of the square from one parent and the circles in the right half from another (fixing the count to n by adding or removing the circle nearest the cut), then run SLSQP on the child. Otherwise start from a fresh random point. Replace the worst pool member when the child beats it.
backlog.title: Elite pool with crossover

backlog.spec: Vary the objective during exploration: for each restart draw random positive weights w_i (for example uniform in [0.5, 1.5]) and maximise sum(w_i * r_i) with SLSQP, then evaluate the true sum of radii after repair. Weighting breaks the symmetry of the objective and can lead SLSQP into different local optima, while the final ranking still uses the unweighted sum.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted random restarts

backlog.spec: Instead of giving every circle the same INIT_RADIUS, draw each initial radius uniformly between 0.01 and 0.12 and then scale the whole set so the total area of the circles is about 0.6 of the unit square. The varied sizes start SLSQP from a less symmetric point, and the rescaling keeps the starting configuration not too overlapping.
backlog.title: Stochastic initial radii

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to a value such as 1000 and set SLSQP options ftol to 1e-12 so the local solver converges fully instead of stopping early at a non-optimal point. Each restart then takes longer, so the number of restarts drops, but each one is better converged. Check that the runtime per restart still leaves several restarts in the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP iteration budget

backlog.spec: Measure the time taken by the first few restarts and their final sums. Use a fixed short budget per restart (for example the mean of the first three restart times times 1.5) and cap restarts so that at least five complete within the time limit. This makes the number of restarts depend on the actual per-restart cost on the grader instead of a fixed count, and avoids wasting the last partial restart.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart time budgeting

backlog.spec: Increase TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to about 0.93 of time_limit, since time.process_time is CPU time on one thread and the harness voids only calls over 45 s against a 30 s limit. Leave a margin for the final repair or LP step, which is fast. This gives roughly 16 percent more search time at essentially no code cost.
backlog.title: Raise the time fraction safely

backlog.spec: Occasionally generate starts with a symmetry: for example reflect a random half of the centres across the diagonal or across the vertical midline, so the start is symmetric about that axis, then run SLSQP on the full set. Many best-known packings of squares have partial symmetry, so symmetric starts sample a different and often better region of the landscape.
backlog.title: Symmetric initial configurations

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, project each initial centre into [r, 1-r] using a radius-aware clip and set initial radii to the distance to the nearest wall or 0.5 times the nearest-neighbour distance, whichever is smaller. Starting from a feasible point lets SLSQP make steady progress instead of spending iterations removing initial overlaps.
backlog.title: Batch clipping and feasibility at start

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and the repair, run a short Nelder-Mead or coordinate search on the radii alone with the centres fixed, only accepting moves that keep the packing valid. This is a cheap post-polish that squeezes out a little sum from each candidate. Keep it short so most of the budget still goes to restarts.
backlog.title: Gradient-free refinement after SLSQP

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK from 1e-9 to about 1e-12 and make the repair check against the harness tolerance of 1e-10 rather than strict zero overlap. This recovers the small loss caused by the fixed shrink of every radius, which over 26 circles adds up to a measurable amount. The final packing must still pass the exact double-precision check with margin.
backlog.title: Smaller shrink margin

backlog.spec: Pick a random subset of about 20 percent of circles from the incumbent, remove them, re-solve for the remaining circles by SLSQP with their positions fixed as starts, then add the removed circles back at random positions and run SLSQP on the full set. This large-neighbourhood move keeps most of a good structure while letting part of it reorganise.
backlog.title: Dropout-style circle removal and reconstruction

backlog.spec: Solve the packing for n+1 circles from the same seed, then delete the circle that contributes the least radius and use the remaining centres as a start for n circles, followed by SLSQP. Also try n-1 and add the largest gap circle. Starting from neighbouring-size optima gives structurally good initial configurations that random starts rarely reach.
backlog.title: Multi-start with different n offsets

backlog.spec: Use an objective of -sum(r) + lambda * sum over pairs of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2, with lambda increasing over the restart (for example from 1 to 1e4). Each restart runs a small L-BFGS-B pass at each lambda value, and the final point seeds SLSQP. This is a soft-to-hard continuation that tends to find better basins than an abrupt constraint start.
backlog.title: Penalty-weighted objective annealing

backlog.spec: Before the final repair, add tiny Gaussian noise (sigma 1e-7) to the centres and then recompute the radii with the LP step so the packing is not stuck at a degenerate constraint point. Accept the noisy version only if its sum is higher. This escapes tight degenerate points where SLSQP stalls at a slightly suboptimal face.
backlog.title: Small random centre noise in repair

backlog.spec: Make each solve call run two independent streams from rng children (np.random.default_rng(seed).spawn(2)) with different start types (random and lattice) and return whichever packing has the larger sum. Since the grader averages three seeds, a diverse portfolio within one call reduces the chance that all restarts converge to the same weak basin.
backlog.title: Best-of-ensemble averaging of seeds

backlog.spec: Precompute the pair index arrays and build all pairwise distance terms with a single fancy-indexed array operation, reusing preallocated buffers in cons and the Jacobian across SLSQP iterations instead of creating new arrays each call. This is a pure speed-up with the same optimisation, giving more restarts within the same budget.
backlog.title: Vectorised constraint assembly

backlog.spec: Impose per-circle upper bounds on each radius that are the distance to the nearest wall, passed as bounds in SLSQP, and a lower bound of zero, rather than only as inequality constraints. Bounds are handled natively by SLSQP and reduce the number of inequality constraints by 4n. This can make the local solver more stable and faster near the boundary.
backlog.title: Shrinking-target radius bounds

backlog.spec: Replace the equal-budget restart loop with a successive-halving schedule. Generate a pool of about 16 random starts, run each for a short SLSQP budget (for example MAX_ITER 40), keep the top half by sum of radii, and continue only those with more iterations. Repeat until the time budget is used, then run _repair on the best survivor. Keep the time check via time.process_time so total CPU stays under TIME_FRACTION * time_limit. This spends more of the budget on promising basins instead of finishing many poor local solves.
backlog.title: Successive halving over random starts

backlog.spec: Build a start for n circles by taking the best packing found for n-1 circles (solved with the same routine, so it is cheap) and inserting one new circle at the largest empty hole. Estimate the hole on a 200x200 grid of candidate points, choosing the point that maximises the distance to the nearest centre minus that centre's radius, with the walls included. Use the hole's clearance as the initial radius, then run SLSQP on all n circles. On alternate restarts fall back to a random start so the search keeps diversity. This is a bolder constructive start than the existing random initialisation.
backlog.title: Largest-hole insertion from the best n-1 packing

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and before the final _repair, identify the active contacts: pairs whose gap is below 1e-7, and circles touching a wall within 1e-7. Treat these as equalities and solve the resulting system with a few Gauss-Newton steps on the centres and radii, leaving unknowns free only where the system is determined. Accept a step only if the sum of radii increases and the packing still passes the exact validity check. The gain is small, but it recovers digits lost to SLSQP's tolerance using a local, cheap step.
backlog.title: Contact-graph Newton polish of the final packing

backlog.spec: Replace the hard non-overlap constraints in the first SLSQP phase with an objective that adds mu * sum(log(gap)) over pair gaps and wall gaps, where gaps are the constraint values and mu starts at about 1e-2. Re-solve while decreasing mu by a factor of 10 each stage, down to 1e-7, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution. Finish with the original hard-constraint SLSQP. The barrier keeps iterates strictly interior, which may steer SLSQP toward better basins than the hard-constraint path.
backlog.title: Log-barrier continuation on the gap terms

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP call, restart SLSQP from its own output and repeat until the sum of radii improves by less than 1e-9 or 5 restarts have run. SLSQP often stops early on a poorly scaled problem, so a warm restart can carry on from where it stopped. Use the same MAX_ITER per call and keep the time check. Only the number of restarts changes, not the constraint set.
backlog.title: Warm-restart SLSQP until convergence

backlog.spec: After a local optimum is found, apply a swap move: pick a large circle and a small circle, exchange their centres while keeping each radius, and re-run SLSQP from this swapped start. Accept the result only if it beats the current best. Try a few random swaps per restart, chosen so that the pair is far apart. Swapping positions of unequal circles can move the packing into a different basin without a full random restart.
backlog.title: Swap moves between large and small circles

backlog.spec: For each start, first solve SLSQP with all radii inflated by a margin delta (for example 0.01) in the non-overlap and wall constraints, so the solution is infeasible but spread out. Then deflate: take the centres, and solve again with the true radii as the starting point. Use a small set of delta values in the outer loop and keep the best valid result. The inflated problem penalises crowding early, which can give a more uniform starting configuration for the true problem.
backlog.title: Over-inflation then deflation

backlog.spec: Use only the best packing found across all restarts as input to a final local optimisation with scipy.optimize.minimize using the trust-constr method, with the same constraints and the analytic Jacobian of the constraints. Run it for the remaining time, then call _repair. Other restarts keep using SLSQP. This tests whether a different local solver reaches a better local optimum from the same start.
backlog.title: Trust-region polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: Initialise each circle's radius from the geometry of its random centre instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS. Compute the Voronoi-like nearest-neighbour distance for each centre (using scipy.spatial.cKDTree on the start centres), then set its initial radius to half the nearest-neighbour distance, capped by the wall distance. Pass this into SLSQP as x0. The start is then nearly feasible from the outset, so SLSQP begins closer to a valid region and may converge in fewer iterations.
backlog.title: Voronoi-based initial radii

backlog.spec: Split the n circles into two groups: a few large circles (about 20 percent) and the rest. Solve first for the large-circle layout only, using SLSQP with the large circles as the variables, and then add the small circles at random in the gaps and run SLSQP on all circles together. This decomposes the search so the large circles, which decide the overall structure, are settled first. Keep the best final packing after _repair, as in the current solver.
backlog.title: Stagewise hierarchical packing by size class

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start with an event-free growth process. Place n centres at random, start all radii at 0, then repeat: move each centre by a small random jiggle (step about 0.01, shrinking over time), and grow every radius to the largest value that keeps the packing feasible. Stop after a fixed number of rounds, then pass the centres and radii into the existing phase-2 free-radius SLSQP. All randomness comes from rng.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger growth starts

backlog.spec: Draw the initial centres from a scrambled Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3, scrambled with a permutation drawn from rng) mapped into [0.05, 0.95]^2, instead of uniform random points. Keep the equal-radius phase 1 and the free SLSQP phase 2 unchanged. The aim is more uniform coverage of the square at the start, so different restarts explore different basins.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Halton starting centres

backlog.spec: Give each restart its own SLSQP iteration cap taken from the Luby sequence (1,1,2,1,1,2,4,1,1,2,...) times a base of 50 iterations, instead of a fixed MAX_ITER of 200. Most restarts stay short, and occasional long runs let hard starts converge. Keep the time limit and the best-of logic unchanged. The schedule is a fixed function of the restart index, so it needs no tuning per run.
backlog.title: Luby-sequence restart budget

backlog.spec: After the time loop, take the best (centres, radii) and run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same overlap and wall constraints, using a finite-difference-free analytic Jacobian of the constraint vector. Give it a small slice of the time budget, reserved from TIME_FRACTION. Accept the polished result only if it is valid under the exact check and its radius sum is larger; otherwise keep the SLSQP result.
backlog.title: Interior-point polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: On half of the restarts, place a fixed number of circles on the four walls first, evenly spaced along each side with random offsets, and then fill the interior with the remaining circles at uniform random positions. The boundary circles start with radius at the wall distance. Then run the same two-phase SLSQP. Packings of this kind have circles touching the walls, which the plain random start rarely reaches.
backlog.title: Boundary-ring-first placement

backlog.spec: Add a quadratic regularisation term to the phase-1 objective that pulls every centre toward a random anchor point drawn from rng, with weight lambda that starts at 0.05 and decays linearly to 0 over the phase-1 iterations. The term spreads the circles out early, and as it fades the true radius-sum objective takes over. Phase 2 keeps the unregularised objective, so the final answer is still judged on the true sum of radii.
backlog.title: Annealed pull toward a random anchor

backlog.spec: Run the cheap phase-1 equal-radius solve for every restart. Keep a running list of phase-1 radii. If a restart's phase-1 value is below the median of the values seen so far (after the first 10 restarts), skip its phase-2 solve and go to the next restart. Only promising starts get the expensive free-radius SLSQP. The rule uses no extra randomness and does not change the best-of logic.
backlog.title: Median-stopping on phase 1

backlog.spec: After the repair step, run a final pass with no SLSQP: visit the circles in a random order drawn from rng, and for each circle set its radius to the largest value allowed by the walls and its current neighbours, leaving the other circles fixed. Repeat the pass until no radius changes by more than 1e-12. The result is still valid by construction and can only increase the radius sum. Apply the pass to the best packing only.
backlog.title: Greedy coordinate radius growth post-pass

backlog.spec: On a subset of the time budget, run scipy.optimize.differential_evolution over the 2n centre coordinates. The objective is the sum of radii computed by a fast greedy repair (radius equal to the minimum of the wall distances and half the nearest-neighbour gap), with a penalty for any centre outside the square. Use the seed for the DE random state and a small population. Then take the best centres and run the existing two-phase SLSQP from them. Keep the result only if it beats the random-restart best.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP local refine

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise an unconstrained energy with scipy L-BFGS-B. The energy is the sum of squared overlap depths (max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2) plus squared wall violations, with radii fixed at a target value that grows from 0.08 to the value that gives feasibility, in steps. Smooth the penalty by averaging the overlap over Gaussian jitters of the centres with a sigma that shrinks over the steps. Pass the resulting centres into the existing SLSQP as a warm start.
backlog.title: Gaussian-smoothed overlap penalty with L-BFGS-B

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the sqrt pair constraint d_ij - r_i - r_j >= 0 with the smooth form ||c_i - c_j||^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0, and add the constraint r_i + r_j >= 0 only where needed to keep the sign meaningful. Use squared distances in both phases and keep the same SLSQP calls. The sqrt has an ill-conditioned gradient when two centres nearly coincide, so this may let SLSQP take longer steps near contact. Leave the repair step unchanged so validity is still enforced by the final shrink.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: After each local solve, fix the centres and solve the radius LP with linprog (HiGHS). Read the dual marginals of the non-negativity and pair-contact rows and sum them per circle to get a sensitivity score. With probability 0.3, remove the circle with the lowest sensitivity (the one whose removal costs least), and reinsert it at the centre of the largest empty hole found on a 100 by 100 grid. Then re-run the two-phase SLSQP from that state. Keep the move only if sum(r) improves, otherwise keep the previous packing. This targets circles that carry little load instead of picking at random.
backlog.title: Multiplier-guided removal and reinsertion

backlog.spec: Draw K = 30 random centre sets per time slice. For each one, score it cheaply by solving only the radius LP with the centres fixed (linprog, HiGHS, a few milliseconds). Run the full two-phase SLSQP only on the top 2 layouts by LP score, and keep the best final packing. The LP value is a valid lower bound on what the layout can achieve with those centres, so it is a sound filter. Set the number of candidates so that the total time stays inside TIME_FRACTION of the budget.
backlog.title: LP screening of random candidate layouts

backlog.spec: After a local solve, build the Hessian-like matrix J^T J over the active pair and wall constraints at the optimum, where J is the Jacobian of the active constraints in the centre coordinates. Take the eigenvectors with the smallest nonzero eigenvalues (the softest modes of the packing). Perturb the incumbent by moving the centres along 1 to 3 of these modes with amplitude 0.02 to 0.05, scaled by a random sign, then re-run the two-phase SLSQP. Accept the result if it beats the incumbent. Soft modes are the directions in which the packing can rearrange most cheaply, so this is a more structured kick than isotropic noise.
backlog.title: Soft-mode perturbation of the incumbent

backlog.spec: After each local solve, identify rattlers: circles whose radius is within 1e-6 of their wall or pair limit has no contacts, meaning no active pair or wall constraint is within 1e-7. Remove all rattlers, and place each one at the grid point that maximises the distance to the nearest centre minus that centre's radius, using a 150 by 150 grid. Then re-run the two-phase SLSQP with the relocated circles as the starting point, and keep the result only if sum(r) improves. Rattlers waste area without adding to the sum, so moving them to holes can unlock slack for the rest of the packing.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation into the largest hole

backlog.spec: Replace the joint SLSQP with alternating block coordinate ascent. Step A: fix the radii and maximise the minimum slack over the centres (a minimax problem, solved by SLSQP over centres and one epigraph variable). Step B: fix the centres and solve the radius LP with linprog to maximise sum(r). Repeat A and B for up to 15 rounds, or until the gain in sum(r) falls below 1e-9. Use the original joint SLSQP only as a final polish. Each block is smaller and better conditioned than the full problem, so the alternation may escape the basins that a joint solver settles into.
backlog.title: Alternating block optimisation of centres and radii

backlog.spec: Run four chains in parallel, each holding a current packing. Each chain takes a step: perturb its centres with Gaussian noise of scale sigma_k, where sigma_k is 0.01, 0.03, 0.08 and 0.2 for the four chains, then run the two-phase SLSQP and repair. Accept the new state with the Metropolis rule on sum(r), using a chain-specific temperature. Every 20 steps, propose swapping the states of adjacent chains with the standard replica exchange probability. Return the best packing seen by any chain. Seeds go to a single numpy generator so the run is deterministic. This is a tempered version of the existing annealing walk and it keeps low-temperature chains focused on local refinement.
backlog.title: Replica exchange across perturbation temperatures

backlog.spec: After each local solve, compute for each circle its slack, defined as the minimum over its wall gaps and pair gaps of the distance minus the sum of radii. Set the kick amplitude for circle i to be proportional to its slack, with a floor of 0.005 and a cap of 0.05. Perturb the centres of the incumbent with these amplitudes and re-run the two-phase SLSQP. Circles with more free room move more, and tightly jammed circles move little. Accept only improvements. This replaces the uniform kick size with one that depends on the local state of each circle.
backlog.title: Slack-proportional per-circle kicks

backlog.spec: In phase 2, optimise sum(r) plus a small linear tilt term eps * (a . x + b . y), where a and b are random unit-scale vectors drawn from the seed generator, and eps starts at 0.05 and decays geometrically to 0 over the phase-2 iterations. Each restart draws its own tilt. The tilt pushes the packing toward a random side of the square early on, so the packing can rearrange large-scale structure, and the final solve has eps = 0 so the objective is exactly sum(r). Repair and validity checks are unchanged. The tilt is a smooth term, so SLSQP keeps the same constraints and its gradient stays well defined.
backlog.title: Random linear-tilt objective annealing

backlog.spec: Solve first with the radii forced to be at most 0.9 times the wall-gap bound of the final problem, that is, with a shrunken feasible set, then relax the cap to 1.0 in three stages by reusing each stage's solution as the next start. Each stage is a full two-phase SLSQP. The shrunken stages give circles room to settle into a global arrangement before the outer constraints bind. Use the final stage's output as the restart result. This is a continuation over the feasible set, not over the penalty weight, and it has no effect on the validity check, which remains exact.
backlog.title: Coarse-to-fine radius-scale continuation

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP phase-2 solve with a sequential linear programme. At each step, linearise every pair-distance constraint, wall constraint and radius bound around the current (centres, radii), and solve the LP max sum(r) with step bounds |dc|, |dr| <= delta using scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS). Accept the step if the true nonlinear feasibility-adjusted sum improves; otherwise shrink delta by half. Grow delta by 1.5 after accepted steps. Stop when delta < 1e-7 or after a fixed iteration cap, then keep the best valid iterate. Keep the equal-radius phase 1 as the start, so the only change is the local solver.
backlog.title: Sequential LP with trust region as local solver

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP solve, optimise a smooth surrogate. Let g be the vector of all pairwise gaps and wall gaps for the current centres and radii (radii as free variables). Minimise -sum(r) + (1/beta) * log(sum(exp(-beta * g))) with L-BFGS-B, which penalises the worst gap smoothly. Raise beta through the schedule 10, 100, 1000, 10000, warm-starting each stage from the previous one. Hand the final iterate to the existing SLSQP phase 2 as the starting point. This is a regularised continuation of the hard max-min problem and it costs little per restart.
backlog.title: Soft-min gap continuation with L-BFGS-B before SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the first 30% of restarts, perturb the best packing with a cluster move. Choose a random line through the square, and split the circles into two sides. Rotate the circles on one side by a random angle in [-0.3, 0.3] rad about the line's midpoint (or reflect them across the line), then remove any centre outside [0,1]^2 by clipping. Run the free-radius SLSQP from that configuration, and keep it if it beats the incumbent sum of radii. This large structured move reorganises whole clusters rather than single circles, which is different from a Gaussian kick.
backlog.title: Slice-and-rotate cluster move on the incumbent

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of four move types: fresh random restart, Gaussian kick of the incumbent, slice-and-rotate of the incumbent, and remove-and-reinsert of one circle. At each step choose a move with UCB1 over its running mean reward. The reward is 1 if the local solve improves the incumbent and 0 otherwise, with a small bonus for a new best. Each move is followed by the same SLSQP solve and repair as now. The bandit replaces the fixed loop, so the search allocates time to whichever move type is currently productive. The code change is one selection rule plus a counter per move type.
backlog.title: Bandit allocation over move types

backlog.spec: Run iterated local search on the incumbent. At iteration k, perturb every centre by independent Gaussian noise with standard deviation sigma_k, where sigma_k decays geometrically from 0.08 to 0.001 across the time budget. Then run the free-radius SLSQP and repair. Accept the new packing only if its sum of radii is above the incumbent. Use the decay as the schedule: large kicks early escape the basin, and small kicks late polish it. Keep the first 20% of the budget for the existing random restarts so the starting incumbent is good.
backlog.title: Geometrically decaying perturbation amplitude around the incumbent

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP solve, run a Langevin dynamics stage on a soft-disk energy. The energy is the sum of squared overlap penalties over pairs and walls, plus a small reward -lambda*sum(r) for radii fixed to the equal-radius phase-1 value. At each step add Gaussian noise of variance 2*T*dt to the centres and descend the energy. Decrease the temperature T geometrically from 1e-2 to 1e-5 over about 2000 steps, then quench with gradient descent. Pass the quenched centres to the existing free-radius SLSQP. The noise lets the configuration cross barriers that a pure SLSQP start cannot cross.
backlog.title: Langevin soft-disk annealing before quench

backlog.spec: Generate the initial centres by Lloyd relaxation rather than uniform sampling. Draw about 4n random points in the square, assign each to its nearest of n seed centres, and move each seed to the centroid of its cell. Repeat 20 iterations, which yields an approximately centroidal, evenly spread layout. Add small uniform jitter of 0.02, clip to [0.05, 0.95], and then run the existing two-phase SLSQP. This gives well-spread starts whose cells are roughly equal, instead of the random layouts the restarts draw now.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal Voronoi starts

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP phase-1 solve, before phase 2, make the configuration feasible with Dykstra-style alternating projections. Repeat up to 200 times: for each violated pair, push the two centres apart along their connecting line by half the overlap; for each circle crossing a wall, push its centre inward. Keep the radii at the phase-1 value, then compute the maximal feasible radii for these centres with the exact LP already available. Use the resulting radii as the warm start for phase 2. This yields a near-feasible start with a usable radius sum, so SLSQP starts from a feasible point.
backlog.title: Alternating-projection feasibility pre-step

backlog.spec: For each restart, run scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on the penalised objective -sum(r) + 50 * sum(overlap^2 + wall-violation^2) over the flat vector of centres, with radii set by the exact LP of the centres. Use bounds [0.05, 0.95] on each coordinate, a maxiter that fits roughly a fifth of the per-solve CPU budget, and seed=rng.integers(2**31). Polish the best centres found with the existing free-radius SLSQP and repair. Dual annealing is a global stochastic optimiser with a different exploration mechanism from random restarts, and it can find different basins.
backlog.title: Dual annealing global search for the small-n regime

backlog.spec: After SLSQP converges, identify the active set: pairs and walls whose gap is below 1e-6. Treat those constraints as equalities and eliminate the dependent variables. Minimise -sum(r) over the remaining free variables with BFGS, using the analytic gradient, and recompute the active set after each accepted step. Accept a step only if the full constraint set stays satisfied to 1e-9. This is a reduced-space Newton-like polish of the local optimum, and it converges more precisely than SLSQP's active-set handling, which may stop short at the contact graph.
backlog.title: Quasi-Newton on the active-constraint manifold

backlog.spec: Keep the simulated-annealing/ILS walk from the slot-8 incumbent, but adapt the perturbation amplitude with a 1/5-style rule. Track the acceptance rate over a sliding window of 20 steps. If it is above 0.3, multiply the amplitude by 1.2; if below 0.15, multiply it by 0.8; clamp to [1e-3, 0.1]. Start from amplitude 0.02. Accept a candidate when its repaired sum of radii is at least the current value minus a temperature that decays geometrically from 1e-3 to 1e-6 over the budget. Keep the best packing seen. Only train.py changes.
backlog.title: Adaptive step size for the perturbation walk

backlog.spec: Run K=3 independent walk chains, each seeded from rng.spawn-style child generators derived from the seed. Each chain runs its own perturbation walk (ILS from a fresh random start for the first 20% of its share of the time, then perturbations of its own current best). Every 25% of the total budget, every chain replaces its current state with the global best packing so far, but only if it is strictly better. Return the global best. The time split is by process_time, as in the current loop.
backlog.title: Two-island model with periodic migration

backlog.spec: Build a start from scratch instead of uniform random centres. Sample 2000 candidate points uniformly in [0,1]^2 each step. For each candidate, the free radius is min(distance to walls, distance to placed centres minus placed radii). Place the candidate with the largest free radius, but with 50% probability choose randomly among the top 10 candidates. Repeat until n circles are placed, each with its free radius. Feed these centres and radii to the existing phase-2 free-radius SLSQP, then repair as usual. Use this construction for about one start in three, and keep random starts for the rest.
backlog.title: Greedy maximal-empty-circle construction starts

backlog.spec: On each restart, with probability 0.5, pin four circles at the corners of the square. Their radii are fixed at a random value in [0.05, 0.2] and their centres are removed from the free variables. Initialise the other n-4 circles uniformly, then run the existing two-phase SLSQP on the free variables only, adding the fixed circles' constraints as constants. Repair and select as before. The point is to test whether corner-anchored basins are a different family from the free-start basins.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored restarts

backlog.spec: In phase 2, change the objective to -(sum r) - mu * sum(log r_i), where r_i is kept strictly positive by the constraint r_i >= 1e-6. Start with mu = 1e-2 and run SLSQP. Then divide mu by 10 and re-run from the result, down to mu = 1e-7 or until the iteration limit. The barrier keeps small circles from collapsing to zero early and lets their centres move to better contacts. Keep the existing contact and wall constraints unchanged, and repair at the end as before.
backlog.title: Radius log-barrier continuation in phase 2

backlog.spec: Maintain an archive of local optima keyed by a coarse bin of their sum of radii (bin width 0.005). Each new restart is either a fresh random start with probability 0.4, or a perturbation of an archived optimum drawn from the least-visited bins with probability 0.6. Perturb by moving 2 random circles to random positions and re-running phase 2. Add the result to the archive and increment its bin count. This spreads effort across distinct basin qualities instead of always refining the current best.
backlog.title: Archive-stratified restart sampling

backlog.spec: Perturbation in a spatial neighbourhood rather than the whole packing. From the current best packing, choose a random point p in the square and a radius R uniform in [0.15, 0.35]. Every circle whose centre lies within R of p gets a new uniformly random centre inside the disc, and its radius is reset to the repaired minimum. Run phase 2 SLSQP on the whole packing starting from this state, then repair. Accept the result if it improves the best. This is a local kick, unlike whole-packing restarts and random drop-out moves.
backlog.title: Local disc re-randomisation kick
